newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti taking legal advice on criticism.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti taking legal advice on criticism.

text.p: Italian information technology group Olivetti said in a statement on Thursday it was seeking legal advice after comments by former director general Renzo Francesconi on the company's first half results.

"Following the comments of...Francesconi to the press regarding the economic results and the capital and financial situation of Olivetti, the company asserts (these comments) are completely unfounded," Olivetti said.
Olivetti said: "Consequently, the company announces it has already instructed its own lawyers to take action in defence of the company's moral standing."
Francesconi, who resigned on Wednesday, one day after chairman Carlo De Benedetti, said he did not agree with some of the company's half year results released earlier this week.
Olivetti, which has not broken even since 1990, announced a pre-tax loss for the first six months of 1996 of 440.2 billion lire ($292 million).
Managing director Franceso Caio on Wednesday expressed surprise at Francesconi's statements, saying the half year figures were made on a strict accounting base.
